references.text: Psalm 22 is a messianic psalm that prophetically describes in detail the suffering of the Messiah – abandonment, mockery, and the piercing of hands and feet – and its fulfillment which Jesus points to when he says it was written that Christ should suffer ([ref:Sal 22:1-32|Psalms 22:1-32]).

Isaiah's suffering servant song describes in detail how the Messiah would suffer, be despised, bear our sicknesses, and be crushed for our transgressions. This is the central Old Testament prophecy that Christ had to suffer, as Jesus explains in [ref:Jes 53:3-12|Isaiah 53:3-12].
"After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will raise us up" – a prophecy pointing to the resurrection on the third day, as Jesus refers to in [ref:Hos 6:2|Hosea 6:2].

Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the fish, which Jesus himself used as a sign of his own resurrection after three days ([ref:Jona 2:1|Jonah 2:1]; cf. [ref:Matt 12:40|Matthew 12:40]).

"You will not abandon my soul to the realm of the dead, nor let your holy one see decay." This psalm by David is interpreted messianically as a prophecy of the resurrection, quoted by Peter in [ref:Sal 16:10|Psalms 16:10] (cf. [ref:Apg 2:27|Acts 2:27]).
Isaiah's third servant song describes the Messiah's suffering – he offers his back to those who strike him – as part of what was "written" about Christ's suffering ([ref:Jes 50:6|Isaiah 50:6]).

Paul summarizes the core of the gospel: that Christ died for our sins "according to the Scriptures" and that he was raised on the third day "according to the Scriptures" – this is exactly what Jesus explains to the disciples in [ref:1 Kor 15:3-4|1 Corinthians 15:3-4].

Earlier in the same chapter, Jesus explains to the travelers on the road to Emmaus that Christ had to suffer these things and enter into his glory, and he interpreted for them what was written about him in all the Scriptures ([ref:Luk 24:25-27|Luke 24:25-27]).
Jesus himself predicts his suffering, rejection, and resurrection on the third day – a prediction that matches exactly what he says in [ref:Luk 9:22|Luke 9:22].
Jesus again tells the disciples that everything written by the prophets about the Son of Man must be fulfilled – he will suffer, die, and rise on the third day ([ref:Luk 18:31-33|Luke 18:31-33]).
Paul explained from the Scriptures that the Messiah had to suffer and rise from the dead, and that this Jesus is the Christ – a direct parallel to Jesus' teaching ([ref:Apg 17:2-3|Acts 17:2-3]).

Paul testifies that he says nothing other than what the prophets and Moses said would happen: that Christ had to suffer and, as the first of the resurrected, proclaim light ([ref:Apg 26:22-23|Acts 26:22-23]).
